title: Docs: operator config examples + inline guidance for mixed-workload scheduler prototype
author: Benji Okafor
release_notes: Add operator-facing docs/config examples for enabling the mixed-workload scheduler prototype (default-off).
body:
## Summary
This PR adds in-code documentation and operator-oriented config examples for enabling the **mixed-workload scheduler prototype** (short/long prompt-aware dispatch) behind a feature flag. No functional runtime behavior changes.

This is meant to reduce enablement churn for SREs / Dedicated operators and to make canary rollouts safer by documenting:
- the exact config keys and defaults
- recommended canary rollout approach (scoped routes / small capacity slice)
- guardrail knobs and what they do (fairness window, starvation bounds)
- what dashboards/metrics to watch and suggested rollback triggers

## Context
We’ve had a few parallel threads where operators asked:
- “Which flag do I flip and where?”
- “What’s the minimal set of knobs we should touch?”
- “How do we ensure it stays default-off for all clusters unless explicitly enabled?”

This doc aligns with the scheduler work landing in runtime 1.19 (feature-flagged) and with the rollout checklist in ENG-4829.

Related PRs:
- #8421 feature flag plumbing
- #8433 two-queue policy implementation
- #8444 instrumentation
- #8462 backpressure by class

## What changed
1) **Config examples (YAML) for operators**
- Added a complete example snippet showing the recommended "safe canary" starting configuration.
- Added inline comments in the example about what each knob does and which ones are safe to leave at defaults.

2) **Inline docs next to config schema/flag definitions**
- Added docstrings/comments to the config schema keys to show:
  - default values
  - whether a field is considered "advanced"
  - what happens under overload

3) **Runbook-ish notes in repo docs**
- Added a short operator guide with:
  - enablement steps
  - verification (how to confirm flag is on for a route)
  - monitoring pointers (metric names, what success looks like)
  - rollback steps (single config change)

## Example configuration
```yaml
# Mixed-workload scheduler prototype (runtime 1.19)
runtime:
  scheduler:
    mixed_workload:
      enabled: false              # default-off; enable only for canary
      classification:
        mode: "prompt_tokens"     # conservative default
        short_prompt_max_tokens: 256
        long_prompt_min_tokens: 512
      dispatch:
        policy: "two_queue"       # short-first with fairness window
        short_queue_weight: 0.85
        fairness_window_ms: 250
      guardrails:
        max_long_wait_ms: 5000     # starvation bound (best-effort)
      overload:
        admission_control:
          enabled: true
          short_queue_max_depth: 200
          long_queue_max_depth: 50
```
Notes:
- The config keys above are examples; this PR documents the *current* names as implemented in #8421/#8433.
- If config differs by environment (Hosted vs Dedicated), the guide calls out where to set it.

## Operator guidance (high-level)
- Start with **enabled=false** everywhere; enable only on a dedicated canary slice.
- Watch p95 for latency-sensitive routes + check long-queue starvation signals.
- Roll back by flipping a single boolean and reloading config.

## Testing
- Docs build / lint
- Config schema validation
- Unit tests (no changes expected)

## Checklist
- [x] Default-off behavior clearly documented
- [x] Example includes a safe minimal set of knobs
- [x] Added metric references for dashboards
- [x] Added rollback instructions

## Risk
Low. Docs/config comments only.

## Follow-ups
- After we finalize metric naming in #8502, we may want to update the guide with the final structured log field names.
- Once canary results are stable, consider adding a short section on recommended thresholds per model SKU (tracked in ENG-4829).

review_conversation:
Sofia Ivanova (review): Please add a callout that the classifier thresholds are *not* intended to be tuned per-customer during canary week 1; we want to keep knobs stable until we see baseline behavior. Also please include a clear rollback section at top.

Benji Okafor (author): Added a "Do not tune thresholds initially" note under Classification, and moved rollback steps into the top "How to rollback" section. Also added a short note that threshold tuning should be coordinated with Scheduling oncall.

Sean Gallagher (review): Can we explicitly list the metrics we expect SRE to pin during canary and add suggested rollback triggers? Our oncall has been asking for this.

Benji Okafor (author): Added a "Canary monitoring" section with the initial metric set (queue_depth, wait_time_ms histogram, max_long_wait violations) and a conservative rollback trigger list. Linked SUP-2194 context.

Julian Moore (review): Please keep metric names consistent with #8444. One of these is using an older prefix.

Benji Okafor (author): Updated metric names to match current runtime prefix and added a short note that names may change until #8502 lands.

Connor O'Brien (review): Please ensure release note explicitly says default-off.

Benji Okafor (author): Updated runtime-1.19 note to bold "default-off" and referenced the flag name.

Omar El-Sayed (approval): LGTM. Thanks for making the knobs/guardrails less mysterious.

Sofia Ivanova (approval): LGTM after edits. This will help canary week a lot.

Sean Gallagher (approval): Approved. Rollback guidance is clear now.
